summary: Implemented a focused orbit-render stability fix by disabling scene-capture temporal render history by default. Root cause is most likely persisted scene-capture view history: BP_CameraSensor final_tone_curve_hdr uses TemporalAA/Lumen and USpSceneCaptureComponent2D persists render state, so scene-off flashlight-only captures can accumulate renderer history across orbit frames despite fixed exposure. Each explicit capture is now marked as a camera cut unless --enable-render-history is supplied.
work_completed: Reviewed the requested orbit collection script, workflow helper, light settings, validation tests, and flashlight docs sections.
Added --disable-render-history/--enable-render-history plumbing to run_orbit_collection.py, defaulting to disabled render history for stable data collection.
Set bCameraCutThisFrame=True before each explicit scene capture when render history is disabled, preserving fixed exposure and the active-illumination trio/output structure.
Kept the workflow helper explicit by passing --disable-render-history.
Updated lightweight tests for render-history CLI behavior and capture camera-cut behavior.
Updated flashlight docs to describe render-history reset behavior and the opt-in comparison flag.

findings.message: The progressive brightness was not caused by auto exposure; auto exposure remains disabled by default and fixed exposure behavior is preserved.
The repeated flashlight state mutation path already reapplies the same enabled/intensity/pose values per frame; the new fix targets renderer view history instead.
Live simulator orbit render validation was not run, per task guidance to avoid full live renders unless cheap and safe.
